items.titel: Water Quality in Drainage and Irrigation Channels of Agricultural Landscapes: A Narrative Review with Bibliometric Analysis
items.samenvatting_bron: Drainage ditches, irrigation canals and multifunctional channels are pervasive features of agricultural landscapes and often represent the only remaining aquatic habitats where natural wetlands have disappeared. This narrative review synthesises evidence on surface-water quality in open channels that are purpose-built or strongly modified by humans, excluding closed subsurface drainage and large navigational canals. The evidence base comprises 36 peer-reviewed studies, predominantly from temperate Europe and North America, complemented by a keyword co-occurrence analysis of 851 Scopus-indexed publications, in which channel-specific terms formed peripheral nodes within five clusters defined by broader themes. The reviewed studies show that hydrological regime, residence time, sediment characteristics and vegetation regulate nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment and pesticide dynamics, so that the same channel may act as a pollution source, transport pathway or biogeochemical buffer. Permanent removal is largely confined to nitrogen via denitrification, whereas phosphorus and sediment retention is predominantly reversible. Evidence for irrigation-dominated, semi-arid and tropical systems, greenhouse gas trade-offs and network-scale functioning remains limited. On this basis, the review proposes a channel typology and candidate functional indicators of water-quality performance as conceptual proposals requiring empirical validation, and discusses them in relation to the Water Framework

items.titel: Decade-long data highlight medium-sized, fast-flowing cold-water streams as important recruitment habitats for European river and brook lampreys
items.samenvatting_bron: European river lamprey Lampetra fluviatilis is a migratory (anadromous) species, spawning in freshwater rivers where it co-occurs with its non-migratory paired species, European brook lamprey L. planeri . Both species are listed under Annex II of the EU Habitats Directive, requiring habitat protection and sustainable management across their distribution ranges. Yet, both species have experienced declines and spatial drivers of larval recruitment remain poorly quantified. Lamprey larvae are known to occupy low-velocity depositional microhabitats, but how these requirements scale across river networks remains unclear. Here, we analysed size-structured populations of lamprey larvae across 177 sites in 32 Latvian rivers using data collected between 2014 and 2025. Higher proportions of smaller larvae, likely corresponding to the youngest age classes, were associated with river reaches of medium-size and small catchment area, moderate and high riverbed gradient and colder temperature. In contrast, larger individuals dominated low-gradient, warm river sections with large catchment area. These findings suggest that the observed longitudinal recruitment pattern may be driven by downstream larval dispersal across river networks and highlight small- and medium-sized, relatively fast-flowing cold-water reaches as important recruitment habitats. items.titel: The courtyard benefits framework: ecological, microclimatic and social contributions to health and well-being
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban densification, climate change, and unequal access to green space have intensified the need for small-scale green infrastructure to support health and well-being. Courtyards are common across many urban and architectural traditions, yet their contributions are often examined separately through architectural, microclimatic, ecological, or social lenses. This scoping review asks: how do urban courtyards contribute to the health and well-being of cities, and how can this evidence inform sustainable and inclusive urban planning? Following the PRISMA-ScR framework, we identified peer-reviewed studies via Web of Science and Scopus and screened them against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. We included and analysed 84 studies thematically. The evidence shows that courtyards contribute to thermal regulation, improved air quality, biodiversity support, social interaction, cultural continuity, and restorative experiences. The most frequent themes were environmental benefits, courtyard typology, thermal comfort, energy performance, green infrastructure, and well-being and health-related outcomes. However, the literature remains dominated by architectural and thermal performance studies, with limited integration of urban planning, equity, public health and well-being, and policy perspectives. items.titel: A Multicriteria Framework for Evaluating Urban Morphology and Spatial Quality Using Landscape Units and Fuzzy-DEMATEL: Evidence from Maringá, Brazil
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban morphology strongly affects spatial quality and residents’ quality of life, yet many assessments rely on aggregated indicators and overlook causal links between street-scale attributes. This study proposes a multicriteria framework that combines Landscape Units (LUs) with Fuzzy DEMATEL to evaluate urban morphology and spatial quality. It integrates visual, spatial, and qualitative dimensions through three descriptor families—Green Areas System, Urban Furniture, and Urban Systems—and 12 descriptors. Five LUs in Maringá (southern Brazil) were selected to represent distinct urban fabrics and development stages. Expert judgments were used to weight families and descriptors and to score each LU. Urban Systems emerged as the most influential family, while Buildings, Road System, and General Tree Planting were identified as key drivers of spatial quality. Clear differences appeared across LUs: LU2, aligned with Garden City principles, achieved the highest score, whereas LU5, a peripheral neighborhood with fragmented vegetation and narrow streets, scored the lowest. Overall, higher spatial quality depends on integrating robust urban systems, well-structured green infrastructure, and adequate public-space amenities. The framework is transparent and replicable, supporting morphology-sensitive urban planning and decision-making.

items.titel: Urban Butterfly Pollinator Biodiversity in Zoological Gardens of the Southwest USA
items.samenvatting_bron: Urbanization and climate change are exerting increasing pressure on biodiversity, particularly in rapidly growing cities of the southwestern United States. While urban development is generally associated with reduced species richness, responses among insect pollinators, including butterflies, are highly variable and shaped by habitat availability, resource distribution, and landscape structure. Concurrently, increasing aridity and extreme heat events linked to climate change pose additional risks to ectothermic organisms such as butterflies. Urban green spaces can function as hotspots, yet the role of zoological gardens in supporting local pollinator biodiversity remains poorly understood. Here, we use community science data from eButterfly and iNaturalist to compare butterfly species richness and diversity within zoos to those of their surrounding urban landscapes across five southwestern USA cities. Contrary to previous work comparing botanical gardens, we found that zoos consistently exhibited low to moderate species richness and diversity relative to comparable areas within their respective cities, falling well below our predetermined hotspot thresholds. items.titel: Human-Ecosystem Coupling Mechanisms and Data-Driven Spatial Optimization in Urban Green Infrastructure
items.samenvatting_bron: High-density urban construction continuously alters land cover, hydrothermal cycles, and habitat patterns, significantly impacting residents' well-being through heat exposure, air quality variations, activity opportunities, and nature contact. Urban green infrastructure, relying on vegetation, water bodies, and soil processes to buffer built-up environmental stressors, serves as a crucial link between ecological resilience, public health, and spatial governance. From a socio-ecological coupling perspective, this paper outlines the complex interaction chain between built-up environmental pressures, ecological process responses, resident exposure, and governance feedback, systematically analyzing the synergy, trade-offs, and equity differences of multifunctional services. Based on this framework, it discusses the advanced integration of remote sensing, street view imagery, spatial machine learning, multi-objective optimization, and urban digital twins in state identification, priority area determination, scheme generation, and dynamic feedback. Existing evidence suggests that green infrastructure performance is jointly shaped by ecological structure, urban morphology, population activity, and governance conditions. items.titel: Introduction
items.samenvatting_bron: This book examines the socioeconomic and environmental dynamics of the Amazon, one of the world’s most vital ecological regions. It highlights how traditional Indigenous and local communities are increasingly threatened by large-scale resource extraction, agricultural expansion, mining, and infrastructure projects. These activities have intensified deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and social conflicts while sustaining economic dependence on global commodity markets. The text underscores the region’s heterogeneity, noting that development pressures vary significantly across countries and subregions. It also emphasizes the need for state regulation, regional cooperation, and alternative models such as community-based forest management and agroforestry. Nevertheless, this book only provides limited coverage of economic development in the Amazon region; further in-depth research is needed to gain a more comprehensive understanding of its socioeconomic conditions.

items.titel: Economy, society, and environmental issues in the Peruvian Amazon
items.samenvatting_bron: Peru is characterized by remarkable socio-cultural and geographical diversity, where pre-Columbian Indigenous traditions coexist with the legacy of sixteenth-century Spanish colonization, resulting in a multilingual landscape where Spanish coexists with official languages such as Quechua and Aymara, alongside numerous Indigenous languages. Geographically, Peru is divided into three major natural regions: coast, highlands, and rainforest, with the Amazon rainforest accounting for approximately 11% of its territory, making it one of the world’s richest countries in vascular plant diversity and the third most biodiverse in South America after Brazil and Colombia. This chapter analyses the gradual integration of the Peruvian Amazon into the national economy through successive waves of resource extraction, rubber, timber, gold, oil, and gas, alongside agricultural colonization, examining how infrastructure expansion, neoliberal reforms, and commodity booms have driven deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and socio-environmental conflicts. Representative cases include the Bagua conflict, illegal gold mining in Madre de Dios, and oil spills in Loreto, which illustrate the tensions between extractive industries and Indigenous rights. It also explores the expansion of oil palm, coffee, and cacao cultivation alongside emerging sustainable initiatives such as agroforestry systems. items.titel: Updated roadmap for novel monitoring technologies
items.samenvatting_bron: This report presents an updated roadmap for the routine implementation of novel technologies in biodiversity monitoring at national, subnational and transnational scales across Europe. It builds on a previous assessment conducted in 2024, drawing on an updated partner survey from 2026 and expert discussions held at the Biodiversa+ Science Fair in Barcelona in May 2025. The report covers six technology groups: bioacoustics, camera traps, environmental DNA (eDNA) and genomics, sensor networks, unmanned aerial vehicles (drones), and remote sensing. It examines deployment, the taxonomic groups and Essential Biodiversity Variables targeted, and the constraints affecting wider implementation. Seven strategic recommendations address coordination, collaboration with the private sector, shared data infrastructure, additional technical expertise, accessible reference databases, integration with established long-term monitoring, and alignment with national and international initiatives and policy requirements.

items.titel: District-level analysis of temperature-related excess mortality in the Netherlands
items.samenvatting_bron: Background: While most epidemiological studies have assessed temperature–mortality associations at broad geographical scales, recent research highlights that temperature-related mortality risks are spatially heterogeneous due to local differences in exposure, vulnerability, and adaptive capacity. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of ambient air temperature on all-cause mortality at the district level in the Netherlands. Methods: A three-stage design was applied to assess the association between daily average air temperature and mortality across 3,116 districts and two age groups (0–74, 75+) for the period 2010–2019. First, a case time series design with distributed lag nonlinear models was used to estimate temperature–mortality associations for 355 Dutch municipalities. Second, municipality-level estimates were pooled using a multivariate meta-regression with municipality-level demographic, socioeconomic, climatological, and topographical predictors. Finally, the meta-regression model was used to downscale the risk estimates to the district level and to estimate standardized excess heat- and cold-related mortality rates. items.titel: Uncovering stakeholder preferences for urban blue-green infrastructure siting: Insights from online swing weights elicitation
items.samenvatting_bron: Blue-green infrastructure (BGI) location choice requires addressing objectives across environmental, ecological, urban, governance, economic and social domains, necessitating stakeholder engagement. However, preference elicitation in BGI planning often relies on single-disciplinary or expert-driven approaches that may overlook differences in priorities across stakeholder groups. The primary aim of this study was to understand stakeholder priorities for BGI planning objectives across three BGI groups: small systems (bioretention, infiltration systems, and swales), large systems (constructed wetlands and ponds/lakes) and urban trees, while the secondary aim was to test and advance a preference elicitation procedure using an innovative online swing-weighting software within a GIS-MCDA framework. Across two case studies in Quebec, Canada, 12 stakeholders in Trois-Rivières and 20 in Montréal representing government agencies, non-profit organizations, and research services, participated in five online workshops. They provided weights on an objectives-based BGI suitability framework. items.titel: Fuzzy Synthetic Evaluation of the Role of Algae-Based Materials for Sustainable Construction in South Africa
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change is impacting ecosystems and infrastructure worldwide, prompting the construction industry to adopt sustainable practices to reduce its carbon footprint. Nature-based Solutions (NbS), such as algae-based materials, are emerging as beneficial alternatives to traditional construction materials. However, research on these innovations in South Africa is limited. This study presents findings from a preliminary assessment of algae-based materials in the country’s construction sector. A post-positivist stance was employed, using a quantitative research design with a questionnaire survey targeting built environment experts. Data analyses were performed using frequency counts, mean item scores, the Kruskal–Wallis H-test, and Fuzzy Synthetic Evaluation (FSE). The findings show low awareness and usage of algae-based materials, with bio-carbon cement as the only widely recognized option. However, the study identifies potential applications of algae in masonry, wall finishes, and concrete for structural elements. FSE indicates that respondents perceived algae-based materials as having significant environmental, social, and economic implications for sustainable construction. items.titel: From Adaptation to Effectiveness: A Systematic Review of Climate Adaptation Measures and their Effectiveness in Urban Areas
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban climate adaptation has expanded rapidly from risk recognition and planning towards implementation, but the existence of an adaptation measure does not by itself demonstrate that climate risk has been reduced. This systematic theoretical literature review examines how urban climate adaptation measures can be assessed from two connected perspectives: applicability- whether a measure is suitable and implementable under particular risk, spatial, institutional and social conditions?and effectiveness- whether that measure produces measurable, durable and equitable changes in the risk pathway. Recent peer-reviewed evidence supported by selected authoritative reports, is synthesized across urban heat, flooding, nature-based solutions, early warning, infrastructure, planning, governance and community-based adaptation. The review distinguishes adaptation intentions, inputs, implementation, outputs, outcomes and longer-term resilience and proposes an applicability-to-effectiveness pathway: climate risk and vulnerability to adaptation option to applicability and implementation to outputs to outcomes to durable resilience. The evidence indicates that effectiveness is conditional rather than intrinsic. items.titel: Integrating Remote Sensing, Multi-Objective Optimization, and Agent-Based Modelling for Nature-Based Flood Mitigation
items.samenvatting_bron: By 2030, pluvial flooding is estimated to cause nearly $500 billion in global damage, affecting 54 million people (UNDRR, 2015) each year. By 2050, metropolitan assets worth around $158 trillion could be at risk of floods. This rising risk has sparked an increased interest in nature-based solutions (NbS), as traditional hydraulic infrastructure may lack the flexibility required to manage more complex flood hazards. This study looks into the use of a data-driven approach to identify and assess the effectiveness of upstream afforestation in preventing pluvial floods. We constructed a thorough computational framework for the Girona/Empordà region of Catalonia, Spain. This framework combines cloud-based remote sensing via Google Earth Engine, multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), multi-objective evolutionary optimisation via NSGA-II, and agent-based flood simulation, which is linked to a reinforcement learning agent based on Proximal Policy Optimisation. The framework functions on two stacked spatial scales. At a regional scale (20 x 20 km), it finds and selects suitable afforestation patches. At a meso scale (1 x 1 km), it simulates flood responses to various afforestation schemes. The findings illustrate the technological viability of combining different methods into a single computing process. Preliminary reinforcement-learning results indicate a directional improvement in simulated flood outcomes.

items.samenvatting_bron: Urban water management challenges in Pakistan are intensifying due to the rapid urbanization, increasing population, rising demand for limited water resources, climate change and inadequate infrastructure. The issues of water insecurity and unsustainable urban development are growing because of water scarcity, depleting groundwater reserves, poor water quality, urban flooding and lack of water governance. items.titel: Reviving Damodar Canal: Integrating Heritage, Craft and Tourism for Sustainable Urban Regeneration in Pirojpur, Bangladesh
items.samenvatting_bron: Water-based landscapes have historically shaped the morphology, economy and cultural identity of settlements in Bangladesh. The Damodar Canal in Pirojpur represents one such socio-ecological system that once functioned as a vital cultural and economic corridor. However, rapid urban transformation, environmental degradation and infrastructural neglect have led to the erosion of its historical identity and functional relevance. This study proposes a design-led framework for revitalizing the canal through the integration of cultural heritage conservation and community-based tourism development along with reviving the canal edge. Adopting a multi-scalar methodology, the research combines spatial analysis, contextual evaluation and urban design interventions at different levels. The research was conducted as part of a studio project in collaboration with the Urban and Regional Planning Department (UDD).The focus is placed on a critical 2 km stretch of the canal between the Baleshwar and Kocha rivers, chosen for its urban concentration. Key proposals include the development of a continuous heritage trail, rehabilitation of craft-based communities, riverfront activation near Baleswar river and the introduction of public amenities. items.titel: Gezinnen en bedrijven bij vliegveld Lelystad moeten weg vanwege uitbreiding defensie
items.samenvatting_bron: Vier boerderijen en zes bedrijven moeten verdwijnen, omdat defensie meer ruimte nodig heeft rond Lelystad Airport. De gezinnen en bedrijven waar het om gaat hebben dat vandaag te horen gekregen. "Ik begrijp heel goed dat dit een waardeloze boodschap is", zegt staatssecretaris Boswijk (Defensie), die later vandaag ook langsgaat bij deze mensen. Defensie gaat hen helpen om te verhuizen naar een andere plek, of betaalt een schadevergoeding. Defensie heeft volgens Boswijk de ruimte nodig, omdat de F-35-gevechtsvliegtuigen vaker moeten vliegen. "Daardoor moet je ook meer trainen en onderhoud doen", zegt de staatssecretaris. "Die ondersteunende eenheden hebben fysieke ruimte nodig." Niet wachten op natuurvergunning Lelystad Airport wordt vanwege de doelen van defensie 240 hectare groter. 40 hectare daarvan is nodig om de start- en landingsbaan langer te maken. Het vliegveld heeft op dit moment nog geen natuurvergunning. "Daar kunnen we niet op gaan wachten en dan dit pas gaan doen", zegt Boswijk. "Dan duurt het te lang."
